quote: And then I have you done as the property owner here. Jody, is there anyone else from the title of the home with you? My wife.
stewart_read: Rep correctly identifies a co-owner but takes the answer as a data point rather than a trigger to include her on the appointment, per protocol.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be deferring spouse-inclusion to the closer since this is a phone-only design review, not a decision meeting — but the schema treats title co-owners as required attendees regardless of meeting type.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to follow every 'is there anyone else on title' answer with a direct ask about scheduling both owners on the appointment, the way the script intends.

quote: I'm not sure what it's made of, to be honest with. It's not a it's not a shake roof.
stewart_read: The main-house roof material was never actually pinned down — customer is uncertain and the rep does not press further or note the ambiguity before moving on, though this matters less here since the planned install target is the garage's metal roof, not the house.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged the house roof irrelevant once the customer specified the garage as the install target, making further probing low-value — a reasonable read given the call's flow.
coaching_implication: When a roof-type answer is inconclusive, the rep should still capture 'unknown / customer unsure' explicitly rather than letting it pass silently, especially since the customer flagged a future house re-roof need.

quote: With the company. Yeah. So I've looked at... The possibility of just doing it myself, but I I wanna get some ideas of what would cost that.
stewart_read: Customer discloses she's researched a DIY solar install and is using this call partly as a cost benchmark against self-installation — a competitive-pricing expectation the rep doesn't probe or flag. Rep's response ('Someone else did it. Yeah. Definitely, don't blame me there') treats it as a joke rather than intel.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged DIY comparison as not a real competitive threat worth digging into on a setter call — but this shapes what the closer will be measured against and is worth a follow-up question or handoff note.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to ask one follow-up ('What kind of numbers were you seeing for doing it yourself?') so the closer walks in knowing the customer's price anchor is a DIY estimate, not a competitor quote.

quote: I know at some point I'm gonna have to replace the roof on my house, but, I wanna keep keep it clean right now.
stewart_read: Customer names a future roof replacement on the house — a live cross-sell trigger for Ion's in-house roofing team — and the rep only responds 'Sure. Yeah. Not a problem,' filing it without bridging to roofing.
alternative_hypothesis: The customer explicitly wants solar on the garage, not the house, so the roof-replacement comment may be seen as out of scope for this appointment — but the schema's roof_replacement_planned signal doesn't require the roof and the solar install to be on the same structure to route to the roofing team.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to flag roof-replacement mentions immediately with the standard bridge line, even when the solar target structure differs, so the roofing team gets the lead.

quote: Perfect. Yeah. That's, that's the one. Yep. It's got the, the one month there and the chart. Awesome.
stewart_read: Once the correct kWh number is finally in hand, the rep confirms receipt and moves straight to scheduling without reflecting the number back to the customer as a hook ('so with usage like that, here's the kind of system we'd be designing') — a missed moment to build anticipation for the appointment.
alternative_hypothesis: Given the multi-round bill-retrieval friction, the rep may have prioritized closing the loop quickly to avoid further customer frustration rather than adding another beat — a reasonable efficiency trade-off.
coaching_implication: Once the anchor number lands, use it as a bridge line into the appointment value, not just a checklist tick.

stewart_read: Customer proactively counter-offers a day when the two initial times don't fit her schedule, showing active investment in getting the appointment booked rather than passive tolerance.
coaching_implication: Note for the rep: when a customer negotiates timing rather than deflecting, that's a signal of genuine intent — worth mirroring energy and moving fast to lock the exact time, which the rep did well here.

quote: Okay. That'll be fine. Super excited to get this out to you, Jody. And, yeah, we'll give you a call Monday at 10AM.
stewart_read: The call ends without the standard button-up elements — no one-hour block mention framed as protecting her time, no explicit 'is that fair?' handshake, no no-driving/computer instruction, and no explicit text-confirmation promise beyond a passing mention of a 'confirmation text.'
coaching_implication: Drill the full button-up checklist as a fixed close-out sequence regardless of how smooth the rest of the call went — smooth calls are exactly where reps skip mechanics because it feels unnecessary.
